title: Grade 6 Science — Tue, May 19
description: Food: Where Does It Come From? — Day 2 of 5: Plant parts we eat
subject: science

questions.question: Which part of the plant is onion?
questions.explanation: Onion is a bulb — layers of thick, modified leaves that store food. It is NOT a root.

questions.question: Which part of the plant is tomato?
questions.explanation: Tomato is botanically a fruit — it develops from the flower and contains seeds.

questions.question: We eat the stem of which plant?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is a stem. We also eat stems of kohlrabi, asparagus, and ginger (rhizome = modified stem).

questions.question: Groundnut (peanut) is which part of the plant?
questions.explanation: Groundnuts are seeds inside a pod. They are an underground pod (fruit) but we eat the seed inside.

questions.question: Which plant part is ginger?
questions.explanation: Ginger is a rhizome — a modified stem that grows underground. It is not a root.

questions.question: We eat the fruit of which plant?
questions.explanation: Mango is a fruit. Radish and carrot are roots; spinach is a leaf.

questions.question: Coconut is which part of the coconut palm?
questions.explanation: Coconut is the fruit of the coconut palm. We consume both the flesh (endosperm) and coconut water inside.

questions.question: Wheat flour is made from which part of the wheat plant?
questions.explanation: Wheat grain is the seed. Flour is made by grinding wheat seeds.

questions.question: Which vegetable is eaten as its flower?
questions.explanation: Broccoli (and cauliflower) are flowers that we eat. The green or white head is a cluster of unopened flowers.

questions.question: Mustard seeds and sesame seeds are examples of:
questions.explanation: Mustard and sesame seeds are crushed to extract cooking oil. Seeds are a major source of edible oils.

questions.question: Which of these vegetables is a modified root?
questions.explanation: Sweet potato is a tuberous root (modified root). Potato and ginger are modified stems; garlic is a bulb (modified leaf).

questions.question: Maize (corn) is the ______ of the maize plant.
questions.explanation: Each corn kernel is a seed. The cob is the part that holds the seeds.

questions.question: Which of the following provides BOTH seeds and leaves for food (from the same plant)?
questions.explanation: The mustard plant provides seeds (for oil) and leaves (sarson ka saag). This makes it a very useful food plant.

questions.question: Apple is the fruit that surrounds the seeds. The seeds of apple are:
options: Poisonous to eat in large amounts (contain cyanide compounds)
questions.explanation: Apple seeds contain amygdalin which can release small amounts of cyanide. They are not recommended for eating.

questions.question: Which plant do we get both coriander seeds (for spice) AND coriander leaves (for garnish) from?
options: Coriander leaves and seeds are unrelated
Only the seeds are from the plant
questions.explanation: Coriander (Coriandrum sativum) provides fresh leaves used as herb and dried seeds used as spice — both from the same plant.
